brief_gesture_description: The person stands facing the camera, raises their right hand to their right ear with fingers and thumb extended in a C-shape mimicking holding a phone receiver, tilts their head slightly toward the hand, then lowers the arm back to the side and returns to a neutral standing posture.

iconicity.rationale: The hand-to-ear C-shape is the universally recognized pantomime of holding a telephone receiver, directly resembling the object and its use.

sensorimotor_imagery.rationale: The gesture evokes the familiar bodily experience of holding a phone to the ear, though the movement is brief and lacks sustained listening or talking motion.

motional_salience_gesture.rationale: The movement is small and contained to one arm and a slight head tilt; the rest of the body remains still, giving low overall dynamism.

emotional_salience_facial_expression.rationale: The face remains neutral and expressionless throughout, with no visible emotion conveyed.

gesture_complexity_fit.rationale: The simple, single-hand gesture matches the concrete, everyday nature of the word 'Telephone' without unnecessary complexity.

cultural_familiarity.rationale: The hand-as-phone gesture is a widely known and commonly used pantomime across cultures.

enactment_potential.rationale: The gesture is easy to perform, requiring only raising one hand to the ear in a C-shape with minimal coordination.

possible_ambiguities: The gesture is brief and could momentarily be mistaken for scratching the ear or adjusting hair before the C-shape is clear.
